svg.title: macOS · Photo viewer / grading editor · Editor tab · Masks card expanded · 1000×700
svg.desc: Mirrors App/PhotoViewerView.swift (editorTab → masksCard) hosting App/Overlay/MasksCard.swift — NEW 2026-09-07 from the Claude Design handoff "Masks as Adjustment Layers" (turn 3). This is the other half of a mask: the MASKS TAB owns its shape (photo-viewer.masks.svg), and THIS CARD owns its GRADE. WHERE IT SITS: between the preset chips and the whole-picture panel — a preset is the look, a masked grade is a correction inside it, and the panel below is the frame as a whole. CLOSED BY DEFAULT: with nothing applied the card is ONE ROW — "Masks" and a ＋ Add menu, nothing else. With grades it carries the count ("2 applied"), a "Manage ›" link to the Masks tab, and a wrapping strip of 48×36 tiles plus a dashed ＋ tile. Every tile carries a hairline: an inverted grade draws WHITE where it selects, and a mask reaching its own edge would otherwise dissolve into the white card (found on the Mac, 2026-09-07). Badges: AUTO top-left for Sky/Land, ⊘ bottom-left for an inverted version, and a 55% #F2F2F7 wash over a grade switched off. The open one takes a 2.5pt accent ring. ADD MENU (native Menu, so it is a real menu on both platforms): groups INTELLIGENT · AUTO, CUSTOM and SHAPES, each mask listed TWICE — "Name" and "Name · inverted", a custom mask using its own inverted name. A version already in the card reads "✓ added" and RE-OPENS the grade it has rather than making a second one: MaskGrade is unique on (mask, inverted), and saying so in the menu is what stops a click looking like it failed. Then a divider and New Linear mask… / New Radial mask… / Manage masks…, which jump to the Masks tab with the tool armed. EXPANDED GRADE (click a tile; click it again or ✕ to collapse): the mask’s name at 15/700 with its kind beneath ("Radial", "Sky · AUTO", "Linear · inverted"), Reset while non-neutral, a 20pt ✕; then Enabled and Show mask with Remove trailing; then the SAME sections and rows as PhotoAdjustmentsPanel — White Balance (Temp, Tint), Light (Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows), Color (Saturation), Effects (Clarity, Dehaze — Dehaze joined the card 2026-09-08: Lightroom’s LocalDehaze imports into a mask, and a value the card cannot show cannot be reset either). WHY THAT SUBSET: a local adjustment is a correction of a region, not a look — the capture-referred controls (Sharpen, Noise Reduction, the owned white) belong to the frame as a whole, and Rotation is geometry. TWO RANGES DIFFER FROM THE WHOLE-PICTURE PANEL, deliberately: Exposure travels ±2 EV, not ±5 (a local lift beyond a couple of stops is a different photograph); and TEMP IS A RELATIVE WARMTH — a mired offset from whatever white the whole-picture grade landed on, not a white of its own, since a region cannot sensibly declare a second illuminant. It travels ±25 mired, about ±1000 K at daylight, and reads in Kelvin ("+452 K"); the field’s full ±150 reads +2687 K a third of the way along and is unusable for the nudge this control is. While a grade is open the panel below gains the eyebrow WHOLE PICTURE (11/600, +0.5 tracking, #6D6D72) so scope is never ambiguous, and the expanded mask’s handles appear on the picture — it can be nudged without leaving the sliders, because a handle takes a drag before the armed-slider gesture does. DRAG ↕ TO ADJUST: clicking a slider LABEL arms it (label turns accent/600 and takes an amber DRAG ↕ chip); a vertical drag on the picture then sets that value at Δ = −Δy / 220pt × range, with a HUD pill naming the scope and the value. Esc releases; a double-click on the label resets the field. Wide layouts only — on a phone the picture is the smaller half of a stacked layout and the gesture would fight scrolling, so the labels do not arm there. RENDER ORDER, and it is the whole point: whole-picture grade → each enabled MaskGrade in list order (masked by its shape, inverted where flagged) → text overlays. Nothing is baked; a MaskGrade is parameters, resolved at render time. Preview and export run the SAME stage (SceneAwareCompositor.composited), which is what makes what the editor shows what the export bakes. STAGED HERE by LL_MASKGRADE=first: a radial "Sun" graded +452 K / +0.35 EV and open, and a linear "Quay lift" applied INVERTED. STATES NOT DRAWN (desc-only): the empty one-row card; the Add menu open; a disabled grade’s wash; the armed-label DRAG ↕ chip and its HUD pill; the WHOLE PICTURE eyebrow and the panel under it, which sit below the fold at 700pt once a grade is expanded. Hooks: LL_EDITOR=<uuid|latest>, LL_MASKGRADE=first|shapes|empty. Verified against the running Mac app 2026-09-07.
